'''Rasmus Johan Michael Hansson''' (born 4 September 1954) is a Norwegian biologist, civil servant, environmental activist and a former national spokesperson for the [[Green Party (Norway)|Green Party]]. He led the Norwegian chapter of [[World Wide Fund for Nature]] from 2000 to 2012. In 2013, he was elected to the [[Parliament of Norway]] as the first representative for the Green Party.<ref name=budstikka>Trude Blåsmo (10 September 2013): [https://www.budstikka.no/valg-2013/hiver-seg-pa-sykkelen-fra-berumsmarka-til-stortinget-1.8061332 Hiver seg på sykkelen fra Bærumsmarka til Stortinget] ''[[Budstikka]]''. Retrieved 11 September 2013 {{in lang|no}}</ref>

Hansson was born in [[Bærum]], and grew up in Oslo.<ref name=budstikka/> His father was the actor [[Knut Mørch Hansson]]<ref>[https://snl.no/Knut_M%C3%B8rch_Hansson Knut Mørch Hansson] Store Norske Leksikon. Retrieved 12 September 2013 {{in lang|no}}</ref> of the Trondheim family Hansson which includes several businessmen and lawyers.<ref>[https://snl.no/Hansson Hansson] Store Norske Leksikon. Retrieved 12 September 2013 {{in lang|no}}</ref>

==Early life==
In October 1976 he and two other ([[Harald Hjort]] and [[Knut Are Tvedt]]) built a dam over the creek in front of the entrance of [[Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate|present-day Norwegian Water Resources and Energy Directorate]].<ref name=Course>{{cite news|title=Helt grønn|newspaper=Aftenposten [[A-magasinet]]|date=13 December 2013|author=Halvor Hegtun|pages=10}}</ref>  (This resulted in their ironic<ref name="Course"/> press release being printed by Aftenposten, under the title "Vandalism on power facilities at Middelthunsfallene": "Upon inspection of the facilities on 23 October partial destruction due to vandalism, was confirmed. The dam has been removed and the water is now running its original course - of no use to society.")

==Activism resulting in imprisonment==
As a student he was among the environmental activists that protested the construction of a [[hydroelectric power plant]] in the [[Altaelva|Alta river]] in [[Finnmark]] during the [[Alta controversy]]. He and a fellow student (Jørn Thomassen) were convicted of sitting down on a road meant for "construction traffic".<ref name=Sitdown>{{cite news|title=Helt grønn|newspaper=Aftenposten [[A-magasinet]]|date=13 December 2013|author=Halvor Hegtun|pages=9–10|quote=Begge ble dømt til bøter for brudd på Vegtrafikklovensbestemmelse mot å sette seg ned på vei beregnet på anleggstrafikk.}}</ref> In court he was sentenced for civil disobedience, and he spent 30 days in [[Oslo Prison|Oslo kretsfengsel]].<ref name=Prison>{{cite news|title=Helt grønn|newspaper=Aftenposten [[A-magasinet]]|date=13 December 2013|author=Halvor Hegtun|pages=9–10|quote=I Alta var han gammel nok, og sonet etterpå 30 dager i Oslo kretsfengsel for sivil ulydighet.}}</ref><ref>Thea Marie Astrup (21 August 2013): [http://universitas.no/studietid/58533/heldiggrisen-rasmus Heldiggrisen Rasmus] ''Universitas''. Retrieved 12 September 2013 {{in lang|no}}</ref> In 2014 [[Aftenposten]] said that "The fines, in the order of [Norwegian] kroner ten thousand were too high for the students so they both chose the option of having themselves imprisoned for a few weeks. It felt okay. Because they regretted nothing."<ref name=TenThousand>{{cite news|title=Helt grønn|newspaper=Aftenposten [[A-magasinet]]|date=13 December 2013|author=Halvor Hegtun|pages=13}}</ref>

==Career==
Hansson has a [[Cand.real.|Cand. real]] degree in biology from the [[Norwegian University of Science and Technology]].<ref>[http://www.mdg.no/kandidat/rasmus-hansson/ Rasmus Hansson] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131109160826/http://www.mdg.no/kandidat/rasmus-hansson/ |date=9 November 2013 }} mdg.no. Retrieved 13 September 2013 {{in lang|no}}</ref> He wrote a master's thesis (hovedfag) on polar bears.<ref>Maria Reinertsen (20. mars 2009): [https://morgenbladet.no/samfunn/2009/i_anledningen_isbjornavtalen#.UjGW3z-Tn-o I anledningen: isbjørnavtalen] Morgenbladet. Retrieved 12 September 2013 {{in lang|no}}</ref>

He has worked as an adviser in the Norwegian and been a researcher for [[Norwegian Polar Institute]] and [[Norwegian Agency for Development Cooperation|Norad]]. He led the Norwegian chapter of World Wide Fund for Nature from 2000 to 2012. Since 2012 he has been leading the Oslo Centre for Interdisciplinary Environmental and Social Research ([[CIENS]]).<ref>[http://politisk.tv2.no/spesial/panelet/person/rasmus-hansson Rasmus Hansson] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131029192443/http://politisk.tv2.no/spesial/panelet/person/rasmus-hansson |date=29 October 2013 }} Politisk Panel, [[TV2 (Norway)|TV2]]. Retrieved 16 September 2013 {{in lang|no}}</ref>

==Parliamentary election==
In the [[2013 Norwegian parliamentary election]] Hansson candidated for the first spot on the party's Oslo ballot against the party's national spokesperson [[Hanna Marcussen]] and narrowly won.<ref>NTB (16 November 2012): [http://www.aftenposten.no/nyheter/iriks/Rasmus-Hansson-topper-Miljopartiets-liste-i-Oslo-7046688.html#.Ujca6z_pyro Rasmus Hansson topper Miljøpartiets liste i Oslo.] Aftenposten. Retrieved 16 September 2013 {{in lang|no}}</ref> The party got 5.6% of the votes in Oslo<ref>[http://www.nrk.no/valg2013/valgresultat/partier/miljopartiet-de-gronne Miljøpartiet De Grønne] Valgresultat. [[NRK]]. Retrieved 16 September 2013</ref> in the election 9&nbsp;September 2013 and Hansson was the only person from the Green Party who got a seat in the parliament as the national result was 2.8% and below the 4% threshold for [[levelling seat]]s. It was the first time that the Greens got a representative in the parliament.<ref>Kjesti Nien and Rolf Lie (9 September 2013): [http://www.aftenposten.no/nyheter/iriks/politikk/Miljopartiet-inne-med-n-stortingsrepresentant-7305309.html#.UjcdsD_pyro Miljøpartiet inne med én stortingsrepresentant] Aftenposten. Retrieved 16 September 2013 {{in lang|no}}</ref>

He was re-elected to the Storting following the [[2021 Norwegian parliamentary election|2021 election]], along with party leader [[Une Aina Bastholm]] and [[Lan Marie Berg]]. The party overall received 3.9% of the vote, just shy of the 4% threshold for levelling seats.<ref>{{cite web | url= https://www.nrk.no/valg/2021/resultat/parti/MDG/ | title= Valgresultatet for Miljøpartiet De Grønne | publisher = NRK | accessdate = 24 October 2021 | language = no}}</ref> In April 2024, he announced that he wouldn't seek re-election in [[2025 Norwegian parliamentary election|2025]].<ref>{{cite web | url = https://www.nrk.no/norge/raja-soker-gjenvalg-til-stortinget-1.16853842 | title = Raja søker gjenvalg til Stortinget | publisher = [[NRK]] | date = 22 April 2024 | access-date = 23 April 2024 | language = nb}}</ref>

==Political priorities==
Hansson argues that consumption in Norway needs to be reduced in order to cope with the environmental challenges. During the 2013 campaign for the Greens he suggested that it would be a good idea if the economic welfare was brought back to the level it was in the 1980s, about half of the current level.<ref>Lars Molteberg Glomnes et al (17 August 2013): [http://www.aftenposten.no/nyheter/iriks/politikk/Miljopartiet-De-Gronne-over-5-prosent-pa-stortingsmaling-7282888.html#.UjcIMj_pyro Miljøpartiet De Grønne over 5 prosent på stortingsmåling] ''[[Aftenposten]]''. Retrieved 16 September 2013 {{in lang|no}}</ref> Among his political priorities are more focus on [[wind power]] and saving the polar bear.<ref name=budstikka />

==Family==
He resides in [[Bærumsmarka]].<ref name=budstikka />

He is married and has three children.<ref name=Family>{{cite news|title=Helt grønn|newspaper=Aftenposten [[A-magasinet]]|date=13 December 2013|author=Halvor Hegtun|pages=12}}</ref>
